question:
In the figure, the area of square \(WXYZ\) is \(25 \text{ cm}^2.\) The four smaller squares have sides \(1\) cm long, either parallel to or coinciding with the sides of the large square. In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(AB = AC,\) and when \(\triangle ABC\) is folded over side \(\overline{BC},\) point \(A\) coincides with \(O,\) the center of square \(WXYZ.\) What is the area of \(\triangle ABC,\) in square centimeters?

[Figure 1](figures/2003_AMC_8_Q25_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The fold replaces the unknown location of \(A\) with the known center \(O\). It leaves \(B\) and \(C\) fixed and preserves area, so \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle OBC\) have equal areas.

The large square has side length \(5\) cm because \(5^2=25\). The upper and lower unit-square steps leave one centimeter at each end of its five-centimeter height outside the span of \(BC\). Consequently,
\[
BC=5-1-1=3\text{ cm}.
\]
The two horizontal unit-square widths between the parallel lines \(BC\) and \(WZ\) make their separation \(2\) cm.

Since \(O\) is the center of the large square, its perpendicular distance from \(WZ\) is \(5/2\) cm. The line \(WZ\) lies between \(O\) and \(BC\), so the height of \(\triangle OBC\) with base \(BC\) is
\[
2+\frac52=\frac92\text{ cm}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\operatorname{Area}(\triangle ABC)
=\operatorname{Area}(\triangle OBC)
=\frac12\cdot3\cdot\frac92
=\boxed{\frac{27}{4}\text{ cm}^2},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
